analyst.summary: IndiGo remains India's dominant airline with roughly two-thirds of domestic passengers, and its underlying (adjusted) profitability held up better in the March 2026 quarter than the headline loss suggests. But the last three quarters show capacity growing faster than passenger demand, ticket yields falling, and load factors slipping, all while the overall domestic flying market itself is shrinking -- and the stock trades at a level that assumes this resolves smoothly. With engine-grounding relief only partial through FY27 and the international long-haul aircraft rollout running behind schedule, we see this as a Hold: a genuinely dominant franchise, but not one offering a margin of safety at the current price into an uncertain near-term print.
